title: The `profile/` shelf and the norms
html:
English | Português (Brasil)

The profile/ shelf and the norms

In the engine config (the operator's ~/.config/opencode), there is a folder that separates two worlds that usually get mixed: the operation resources the AI reads and the data that is only yours. The profile/ shelf is the kit's answer to "where does the AI look for operation context without me exposing personal data?".

What lives there

Two kinds of content, different owners. The kit-canonical resources — written by the kit, managed by the content manifest: the per-stack boilerplate registry (profile/stack-templates.yaml, which gm-stack-boilerplate uses to scaffold new projects) and the integrations (the Context7 reference, for example — context7.md). And the personal-by-design definitives: profile/client-profile.md (the org, the products, the client's preferences) and profile/operator-profile.md (who you are, role, e-mail) — versioned NEVER: personal.json designates what is personal and the kit never rematerializes them. The golmet template <client-profile> emits the skeleton for you to fill — templates live in the kit, the config carries only the definitives.

The norms: the house way, with a trigger

The norms — how MinhaOrganizacao does deploy, how a new repo is created — do not live in the config: they live IN-PLACE in the org's state pack (packs/<id>/rules/), one norm per file, in the canonical format of gm-rule-keeper: a title and an explicit trigger at the top.

# MinhaOrganizacao deploy

> Trigger: WHEN creating a deploy pipeline, read this file

The trigger is what makes the norm alive: the workflow's AGENTS.md indexes the norms by trigger, and the AI reads them at work time — when it is about to create the pipeline, the trigger fires and the norm arrives in context. Not documentation to re-read: documentation that arrives at the right time.

The cycle: edit the pack working copy → golmet pack publish (commit + push) → the team runs golmet pack update and inherits. The kit never discards local accumulation — the operator's learning is an organizational asset (the full ecosystem in knowledge.md).
